title: Interactive Rebase Basics
description: Master the interactive rebase workflow, the rebase todo list, and all core actions: pick, reword, edit, drop, and squash.

data.text: Interactive rebase is the Swiss Army knife of Git history editing. It opens an editor listing commits and available actions. You tell Git how each commit should be treated, and Git replays the history accordingly. Mastering it is essential for producing clean, reviewable commit histories.

data.title: Never rebase shared commits
data.text: Only rebase commits that have not been pushed to a shared branch. Rewriting public history causes divergence, forces everyone to re-sync, and can lose work.

The basic form is git rebase -i <upstream>, where <upstream> is usually a commit reference like HEAD~5 or a branch name. Git opens your editor with a todo list showing each commit in chronological order.

data.title: Start an interactive rebase
data.code:
# Rebase the last 5 commits
git rebase -i HEAD~5

# Rebase a feature branch onto main
git rebase -i main

# Abort a rebase that went wrong
git rebase --abort

# Skip remaining commits and continue the rebase
git rebase --skip

data.text: Each line in the todo list has the format: <action> <commit-hash> <commit-message>. The default action is pick. Lines can be reordered, actions changed, or lines removed entirely to drop a commit.

data.title: Rebase todo list example
data.code:
pick abc1234 feat(auth): add login endpoint
reword def5678 fix(auth): validate email format
squash ghi9012 fix(auth): edge case validation
edit jkl3456 feat(api): add user profile route
drop mno7890 wip: temporary experiment

# Lines above are shown in the editor with comments explaining each action

data.title: Available actions
items: **pick** (p) — Include the commit as-is. Use this for clean commits in the correct order.
**reword** (r) — Include the commit but edit its message. The changes stay the same.
**edit** (e) — Include the commit but pause to let you modify it. You can amend, add files, or split it.
**squash** (s) — Combine this commit into the previous one. Git will merge both messages.
**fixup** (f) — Like squash, but discard this commit's message entirely.
**drop** (d) — Remove the commit from history entirely.

data.text: The edit action pauses the rebase at that commit. You can then use git reset HEAD~ to unstage the changes, add them back selectively with git add -p, and create multiple smaller commits. This is how you split a large commit into logical pieces.

data.title: Split a commit during interactive rebase
data.code:
# Step 1: Mark commit as 'edit' in the rebase todo list
# Step 2: When rebase pauses at that commit
git reset HEAD~

# Step 3: Stage and commit changes in logical chunks
git add -p src/auth/LoginService.cs
git commit -m "feat(auth): add login service"

git add -p src/auth/TokenValidator.cs
git commit -m "feat(auth): add token validation"

# Step 4: Continue the rebase
git rebase --continue

data.title: Force push with lease after rebase
data.text: After rebasing a branch that is already on the remote, use git push --force-with-lease. This protects against overwriting teammates' work if they pushed while you were rebasing.

items.question: What is the difference between rebase -i and rebase --interactive?
items.answer: They are the same. git rebase -i is the short form of git rebase --interactive.

items.question: Can I rebase a branch that is not checked out?
items.answer: Yes. Use git rebase -i <upstream> <branch> to rebase an arbitrary branch without checking it out first.

items.question: What if the rebase encounters a conflict?
items.answer: Git pauses and shows the conflicting files. Fix them, stage with git add, then run git rebase --continue. Use git rebase --abort to cancel.

items.question: Can I undo an interactive rebase?
items.answer: Yes, if you have not run git gc. Use git reflog to find the original HEAD position and reset to it: git reset --hard HEAD@{n}.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Interactive rebase opens a todo list for rewriting recent commit history
Use pick, reword, edit, squash, fixup, and drop to shape each commit
Only rebase commits that have not been pushed to a shared branch
edit pauses the rebase so you can modify or split a commit
git rebase --abort cancels the rebase and restores the original state
